name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
aliases: E471, mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids, glyceryl monostearate, glyceryl monopalmitate, glyceryl monooleate, monostearin, monopalmitin, monoolein, GMS, mono- y diglicéridos de ácidos grasos
what_is: A widely used emulsifier made from glycerol and fatty acids. It helps fat and water stay mixed and is found in products such as sliced bread, margarine, ice cream and baked goods. Its fatty acids may come from plants or from animals, and the label does not name the source.
why_botia: If the source is animal, it may be pork, or an animal not slaughtered according to Islamic rules — the label cannot settle it, only a certificate or the manufacturer can. In the NutriNet-Santé cohort, which followed 92,000 adults for years, those with the highest E471 intake had more cancer diagnoses than those with the lowest: breast cancer in women, prostate cancer in men.
can_1: Detect E471 and its common mono- and diglyceride names on an ingredient list.
can_2: Explain that the fatty-acid source may be plant or animal.
cannot_1: Determine from the name E471 whether the fatty acids came from plant or animal material when the manufacturer does not disclose the source.
cannot_2: Determine the amount of E471 or the exact mono-/diglyceride composition from the ingredient list.

title: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
description: E471 is a widely used emulsifier digested like dietary fat. JECFA assigned no numerical ADI; BOTIA flags source traceability because its fatty acids may be plant- or animal-derived.
